status.description: What the loop ended up with. 'optimized' means it kept a kernel that compiled, passed its tests and beat the baseline; 'invalid_input' and 'failed' are the ways it can end with nothing to hand back. 'no_speedup' means kernels compiled and passed, but none beat the baseline in the harness's paired timing: the fastest attempt's measurements come back so the caller can see by how much, and the caller keeps the baseline rather than integrating it. 'needs_input' means the loop stopped before its first iteration for a setting only the user can give -- a `gke_job` profile with no `staging_bucket`, say, which cannot bring profile traces back -- and `summary` carries the question and the setup command. Only the fields a given outcome can actually produce are required -- the measurements are owed by 'optimized' and 'no_speedup' alone, declared in `status_requires` and enforced by the runtime, because this validator has no conditional keywords.

slot.description: The slot this kernel's artifacts live in, `artifacts/tpu-kernel-development/<slot>`. Returned by every result after the loop resolved a slot, so a caller continuing the same kernel passes it back as the request's `slot` instead of relying on matching the path and op again.

base_kernel_path.description: The kernel's input file, as the loop keyed it: the request's `base_kernel_path`, normalized, or, for a request that carried `base_kernel_source`, the file the loop wrote the text to. Returned with `slot`. A caller continuing the kernel passes it back as `base_kernel_path`, with `slot` -- never the text again.

same_file_slots.description: The session's other slots that are the same file as this result's kernel -- the same `base_kernel_path`, or the same resolved real path, which catches one file reached through a symlink -- each with its `target_op`; omitted when there are none. Two kernels can live in one file, so the loop opens a new slot rather than refusing; but a caller that renamed the op, or re-spelled the path, of a kernel it meant to continue sees here that it started over, and can delegate again with that kernel's `slot`.

summary.description: Short prose for the caller. Not the deliverable: the numbers belong in the typed fields and the code in an artifact.

artifacts.description: Durable artifact paths produced under the run's artifacts directory.

best_kernel_artifact.description: Path to the fastest kernel the loop kept. Owed by an 'optimized' result. On a 'no_speedup' result, the fastest attempt, which did not beat the baseline and is not to be integrated.

baseline_latency_ms.description: What the incoming kernel measured, so the speedup below can be checked rather than taken on trust.

best_latency_ms.description: What the best kernel measured. Owed by an 'optimized' or 'no_speedup' result.

speedup_factor.description: baseline_latency_ms / best_latency_ms. Owed by an 'optimized' or 'no_speedup' result.

iterations_run.description: How many iterations actually ran. Owed by an 'optimized' or 'no_speedup' result; it can be lower than the requested budget only if the loop stopped early, which is a fault worth seeing.

iterations.description: Per-iteration record -- the table the loop already reports at the end, returned as data rather than as prose.

latency_ms.description: Absent when the iteration never got far enough to be timed.

speedup.description: This iteration's measured speedup over the baseline, from the harness's paired base-vs-optimized timing in a single process, of the kernel as the iteration left it -- after autotuning, when a configuration was applied. Reported per iteration rather than only at the end because the loop branches on it: above 1.0 the next iteration's planner builds on this kernel and the loop may keep it as its best, at or below 1.0 the planner restarts from the baseline and the kernel is never kept. Absent when correctness failed and the harness printed no timing line.

base_choice.description: Which source this iteration was built from -- `base`, `iter<k>`, or `unknown` when the plan did not say. Makes the loop's trajectory readable: three iterations in a row choosing `base` means each attempt was abandoned, which a column of latencies alone does not show.

profile_summary.description: Path to the iteration's profile report. Absent -- not null -- when the iteration did not compile or failed its tests, because there was nothing worth profiling.

input_language.description: What the primary input was, after classification. `specification` is absent on purpose: an approved synthesized baseline becomes one of these two before any iteration runs, so reporting it here would describe how the run started rather than what it measured. `cuda` is absent because CUDA is never a primary -- it reaches a run only through `reference_paths`, and what it contributed is reported in `reference_trust` instead.

baseline_verified.description: Whether the JAX baseline every number below is measured against was checked against values captured from the caller's own source. Null means no such check was possible -- a jax primary (where the baseline IS the caller's code), or a degraded capture. A speedup against an unverified port and one against a gated port are not the same claim, and a caller reading only `speedup_factor` has no way to tell them apart.

reference_trust.description: How closely a supplied reference kernel matched the primary computation. Absent when no reference was supplied, which is the common case. `rejected` means the reference computed something else and contributed nothing -- a normal outcome, not a failure.

error_message.description: Why the stage did not reach 'optimized' or 'no_speedup'. The unhappy case belongs in the contract, not only in the summary prose.

failure_reason.description: The cause, on the axis the status enum deliberately does not cover. The same vocabulary the stage results use, so a failure that propagates up from a stage keeps its reason.

examples.summary: Kept iteration 3: block-wise softmax with a fused epilogue, 2.31x over the baseline.
